title: A Trip to the City Museum
description: A class visits a history museum and a boy finds a special object.
instructions: Read the text about a class trip to a museum, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: On Friday morning, Mr Lopez took his class to the City Museum. The students travelled there by bus, and the trip took forty minutes. Most of them were excited because it was their first visit. Leo, a quiet boy, brought a small notebook and two pencils.

The museum had five big rooms. In the first room, there were old coins, cups and plates from many years ago. A guide called Mrs Hall told the students about life in the city long ago. Leo wrote down everything she said in his notebook.

In the last room, Leo saw an old wooden toy horse. It was more than two hundred years old, but it looked almost new. Mrs Hall said that a child once played with it every day. Leo drew a picture of the horse very carefully.

Back at school, Mr Lopez asked the students to write about the trip. Leo's story was the longest in the class, and it had his drawing too. Mr Lopez put it on the classroom wall. Now Leo wants to visit the museum again with his parents.

Two weeks later, Leo and his parents went to the City Museum on a Saturday. This time, the museum was very busy with families and tourists. Leo was the guide for his parents. He showed them the old coins and plates and told them everything he remembered from Mrs Hall. His father was surprised, because Leo usually did not talk very much.

Then they went to the last room to see the wooden horse. Mrs Hall was there with another group of visitors. She remembered Leo and his notebook. When she heard about his story on the classroom wall, she was very pleased. She told him that the museum was planning a drawing competition for children in the summer.

Leo entered the competition with a new picture of the toy horse. He worked on it for three weekends, and it was bigger and more colourful than his first drawing. He did not win first prize, but he came second. Now his picture hangs in the museum next to the real horse, and Leo visits it whenever he can.
